capability: Fox-Flory-Whitten (1948-1954) physical scaling-law baseline vs ML comparison for polymer melt viscosity. Second KPI on the same polymer-safe test set as the prior conformal+AD receipt, directly answering the standard red-team challenge 'does your ML actually beat the classical η ~ Mw^3.4 scaling law?'. HONEST FINDING: physical baseline B3 (log η = a + b × log Mw + c × 1/T) at R² +0.5972 BEATS full HistGBM ML (R² +0.4536) by +0.1436 R² on the polymer-safe test (n=194). Classical polymer physics beats ML for melt-viscosity generalization to novel chemistries in this dataset.

b1_ffw_pure_mw_34.prediction_rule: y_pred = offset + 3.4 × log10(Mw); offset = mean(y_train) - 3.4 × mean(log10 Mw_train). Berry-Fox 1968 universal entangled melt scaling.

b2_ffw_linear_mw_only.prediction_rule: y_pred = intercept + slope × log10(Mw); intercept, slope fit by OLS on train.

b3_ffw_linear_mw_and_arrhenius_T.prediction_rule: y_pred = intercept + slope_Mw × log10(Mw) + slope_1/T × 1/T; fit by OLS on train.

b4_full_ml_histgbm.prediction_rule: HistGradientBoostingRegressor with same hyperparameters as parent Polyverse melt viscosity receipt.

metrics.name: best_physical_ffw_baseline_beats_ml_r2_documented
metrics.note: HONEST FINDING: physical Fox-Flory-Whitten baseline with Arrhenius T (B3, R² +0.5972) BEATS ML full HistGBM (R² +0.4536) by +0.1436 R² on the identical polymer-safe test set (n=194). Passing this gate acknowledges the finding: for melt viscosity generalization to novel polymer chemistry, classical polymer physics (Fox-Flory 1948, Whitten 1954, Berry-Fox 1968, Ferry 1980) outperforms ML with 519 features.

metrics.name: ffw_pure_mw_scaling_beats_constant_baseline
metrics.note: Sanity check: pure Fox-Flory-Whitten η ~ Mw^3.4 (1 fitted intercept parameter) at R² +0.3550 beats constant mean R² -0.0009. Confirms the physical scaling law captures real signal even with the classical Berry-Fox 3.4 exponent.

metrics.name: fitted_Mw_slope_close_to_theoretical_range
metrics.note: Fitted Mw slope from B2 (log η = a + b × log Mw) is +2.1107. Falls between the theoretical unentangled-melt exponent (a=1, Rouse regime) and the entangled-melt exponent (a=3.4, reptation regime). Value between 1 and 4 confirms the fitted slope is physically reasonable for a mixed dataset spanning both regimes.

metrics.name: b2_linear_mw_regression_beats_b1_pure_scaling
metrics.note: Fitting the Mw slope (B2, R² +0.5923) improves over the fixed 3.4 assumption (B1, R² +0.3550) by +0.2373 R². Confirms the dataset spans both entangled and unentangled regimes; a single global exponent is suboptimal.

metrics.name: b3_adding_arrhenius_T_improves_b2
metrics.note: Adding Arrhenius 1/T dependence (B3, R² +0.5972) marginally improves over Mw-only linear (B2, R² +0.5923) by +0.0048 R². The small gap suggests the dataset's T range doesn't strongly drive viscosity variance once Mw is controlled — mostly because different sources report measurements at their preferred T rather than systematic T sweeps per polymer.

metrics.name: ml_beats_constant_baseline
metrics.note: Sanity check: ML full HistGBM R² +0.4536 does still beat constant R² -0.0009. ML has learned some signal — just not as much as the physical scaling law captures on this polymer-safe test set.

metrics.name: n_physical_baselines_with_zero_or_few_fitted_parameters
metrics.note: Three physical baselines are evaluated: B1 (1 param), B2 (2 params), B3 (3 params). All draw on published Fox-Flory-Whitten scaling theory (Fox-Flory 1948, Whitten 1954, Berry-Fox 1968, Ferry 1980, Doi-Edwards 1988). Cannot cheat via train/test leakage — only physical variables (log Mw, 1/T) are used.

population: Same population as prior Polyverse melt viscosity conformal+AD receipt: polymer-safe 60/20/20 partition by unique SMILES, 863 train rows and 194 test rows with valid Mw (required for FFW baselines B1-B3). Test polymers (13) are novel chemistry relative to train (41).
split_methodology: Same polymer-safe 60/20/20 partition by unique SMILES under np.random.default_rng(seed=0) as the conformal+AD receipt. All baselines evaluated on the identical test subset (rows with valid Mw). Physical baselines (B1 pure Mw^3.4, B2 fitted-slope Mw, B3 Mw + Arrhenius T) use only physical variables (log Mw, 1/T) — no ML feature engineering.
